step1_figure.schematic_figure: Figure 26.24 (closed-loop step response test circuit) and Figure 26.22 (basic two-stage op-amp schematic)
step1_figure.circuit_type: Fully-differential two-stage CMOS operational amplifier without CMFB in a closed-loop feedback test configuration
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.24 depicts the test setup where the basic two-stage op-amp from Figure 26.22 is configured with 20k feedback resistors (R1-R4) and 250 fF load capacitors (C3, C4) to evaluate step response and settling time. The internal core of the op-amp consists of a cascode-load differential input stage followed by a class-AB output stage with 50 fF Miller compensation capacitors.

quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD by the op-amp core and bias generator

source.reference: Text discussion under 'Adding a Second Stage'

equation.explanation: There are 8 vertical branches in the core op-amp each carrying roughly 20 uA under quiescent conditions, plus the bias circuit branch currents (~50 uA).
equation.assumptions: VGS = 400 mV, VDS = 100 mV nominally per branch

sky130_expected.calculation: With 8 branches at 20 uA: I_core = 8 * 20 uA = 160 uA. Adding bias circuit (~50 uA), total current is approximately 210 uA. For Sky130 at VDD = 1.8 V, with nominal (W/L) sizing, branch currents are 20 uA to 30 uA, giving 160 uA to 250 uA core current.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Device sizing (10/1 NMOS, 20/1 PMOS) with wide-swing cascode bias yields ~20 uA per branch.

quiescent_power.description: Quiescent power dissipation of the op-amp including bias generator

source.reference: Text discussion under 'Adding a Second Stage'

equation.explanation: DC supply voltage multiplied by total supply current under quiescent conditions.

sky130_expected.calculation: P_diss = 1.8 V * 210 uA = 378 uW (core alone: 1.8 V * 160 uA = 288 uW).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Product of 1.8 V supply and nominal 210 uA current.

slew_rate.description: Op-amp slew rate limited by first-stage tail current charging the compensation capacitor

equation.explanation: Maximum differential voltage rate of change when the diff-pair fully steers tail current into the Miller compensation capacitor Cc.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Class-AB output stage does not limit output slew rate when driving load capacitance, leaving the first-stage Cc charging as the primary limit.

settling_time.description: 1% settling time of the closed-loop differential output in response to an input differential step

equation.explanation: Time required for the differential output (vop - vom) to settle to within 1% of its final value following an input step.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text states settling time is approximately 2.5 ns in Fig. 26.24, influenced by the input RC time constant (20k * 25 fF = 0.5 ns) and loop bandwidth.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Directly specified in the text as approximately 2.5 ns.

input_rc_time_constant.description: RC time constant associated with feedback resistor charging the op-amp input parasitic capacitance

equation.explanation: Time constant formed by the 20k source/feedback resistor and the input parasitic/gate capacitance of the op-amp input pair.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Given explicitly in textbook text as 0.5 ns.

closed_loop_gain.description: Differential closed-loop DC voltage gain with 20k feedback and input resistors

equation.explanation: Ratio of feedback resistance to input series resistance for the fully-differential inverting closed-loop amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: |A_CL| = 20k / 20k = 1.0 V/V (0 dB). Differential input swing of 400 mV peak results in differential output swing of ~400 mV peak.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Equal valued matched resistors determine the closed-loop differential gain.

first_stage_gain.description: Voltage gain of the first-stage cascode differential amplifier

equation.explanation: Small-signal differential gain of the telescopic cascode input stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: In Baker's design A_v1 ~= 40 V/V (~32 dB) as shown in Fig. 26.21.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Diff-amp DC gain is confirmed in Fig. 26.21 as approximately 40.

second_stage_gain.description: Voltage gain of the class-AB output buffer stage

equation.explanation: Voltage gain of the second-stage push-pull / class-AB driver.

sky130_expected.calculation: Second stage gain is stated in the text as approximately 10 V/V (20 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Class AB output stage provides approximately 10x gain.

open_loop_gain.description: Open-loop differential DC voltage gain of the complete two-stage op-amp

equation.explanation: Product of first-stage cascode gain and second-stage class-AB gain without resistive loading.

sky130_expected.calculation: A_OL = 40 * 10 = 400 V/V (approx 500 V/V shown in Fig. 26.23 deriv plot, ~54 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Peak derivative in Figure 26.23 is approximately 500 V/V.

differential_output_swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential output voltage swing range

equation.explanation: Difference between maximum differential output and minimum differential output swing.
equation.assumptions: Rail-to-rail single ended swing gives +/- VDD differential swing

sky130_expected.calculation: Single-ended output swings rail-to-rail from ~0.1 V to 1.7 V. Differential swing is from -(1.8 - 0.2) to +(1.8 - 0.2) = -1.6 V to +1.6 V (3.2 Vpp diff) for 1.8V VDD.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Doubling in output swing for fully differential architecture.

step3_testbench.description: Transient and operating point simulation matching Figure 26.24 to measure quiescent power, slew rate, closed-loop gain, and settling time with 20k resistors and 250 fF load caps.
